name: Correlated Error: Phishing Campaign Misclassification

environment_shifts.description: CORRELATED ERROR SCENARIO: Sophisticated spear-phishing campaign using legitimate O365 domains. Campaign alerts look like isolated credential_access events individually. 80% of analysts classify campaign alerts as routine credential_access (auto-close) rather than coordinated attack (escalate). The ERROR IS CORRELATED — all analysts make the SAME systematic mistake because the campaign is designed to evade per-alert analysis. The correct classification only becomes apparent from cross-alert correlation that individual analysts cannot perform in real-time. This tests whether N correlated wrong overrides push the credential_access/auto-close centroid catastrophically toward the phishing pattern.
RECOVERY PHASE: Post-campaign normal operations. Tests whether centroids recover from correlated drift within 2× N_half decisions after campaign ends.

business_context: THE HIGHEST PRIORITY STRESS CASE. During Days 20-30, credential_access volume is 2.5× normal. 80% of analyst overrides on campaign alerts push credential_access centroids in the WRONG direction (toward auto-close for what should be escalated). All 5 analysts make the same error because the campaign is designed to look benign alert-by-alert. This is √N × worse than independent errors. GATE: conservation monitor fires AMBER within 14 days of campaign onset. Centroids recover within 28 decisions (2× N_half) after campaign ends. Asymmetric η limits campaign-period drift.

name: Correlated Error: Ransomware Volume Spike

asset_criticality.note: Mixed medical device and IT assets

device_trust.note: Medical devices with outdated firmware, BYOD clinical

environment_shifts.description: CORRELATED VOLUME SCENARIO: Ransomware incident. All analysts correctly escalate lateral_movement and data_exfiltration alerts — the ERROR is not in classification but in VOLUME overwhelming category distribution. lateral_movement goes from 18% to 55% of all alerts. Centroids for OTHER categories starve because analyst attention is consumed by the incident. credential_access and insider_threat get almost no verified decisions for 14 days.

business_context: VOLUME CORRELATION stress case. During a ransomware incident, classification is CORRECT (analysts escalate appropriately) but volume DISTRIBUTION shifts dramatically. Lateral_movement and data_exfiltration dominate. Other categories starve. Tests: (1) Does conservation law fire for starved categories (credential_access gets V≈9/day instead of 30/day)? (2) Do starved category centroids DEGRADE from lack of updates? (3) After incident resolves (Day 29+), how quickly do starved categories resume convergence? This is a DIFFERENT correlated error than 2D-CE1 — the error is in resource allocation, not classification.
